## Simple explanation

A webhook is an automatic message one service sends to another when an event
occurs, instead of the receiver repeatedly checking for updates.

## Technical explanation

A webhook provider sends an HTTP request, usually with a payload describing
an event, to a configured receiver endpoint. Reliable implementations
authenticate requests, validate signatures and timestamps, handle retries and
duplicate deliveries, and return a response promptly. Delivery is commonly
at-least-once, so consumers should be idempotent.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Webhooks connect model pipelines to data ingestion, job completion,
human-review, and deployment workflows. They enable event-driven integration
but also create an externally reachable surface that must be validated and
monitored.

## How it works

Register a receiver URL with an event provider. On an event, the provider
posts a signed payload; the receiver verifies it, records or queues the event,
and responds with an appropriate status. Longer processing should usually be
handled asynchronously after durable receipt.

## Practical example

When a model evaluation job completes, a pipeline can send a webhook to a
deployment service. The receiver verifies the signature, checks the run ID,
and queues a deployment review rather than trusting the incoming message to
deploy immediately.

## Common misconceptions

- A webhook is not a guarantee of exactly-once delivery; retries can cause
  duplicates.
- HTTPS alone does not authenticate the sender or validate event contents.
